The Pro's & Con's of the 4th Industrial Revolution

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We look at the pros and cons of the 4th Industrial Revolution

Unique Selling Point:
From contact centres to production lines, artificial intelligence in the workplace can bring about great efficiency, faster services, and quick turnaround times for customers. For business owners, AI helps eliminate human error, waste and costs. But for workers, the fourth industrial revolution spells great unease and uncertainty. Carte Blanche unpacks the prospects for employees when automation threatens jobs in a country with nearly 30% unemployment.

Press Release:


From contact centres to production lines, artificial intelligence in the workplace can bring about great efficiency, faster services, and quick turnaround times for customers. For business owners, AI helps eliminate human error, waste and costs. But for workers, the fourth industrial revolution spells great unease and uncertainty. Carte Blanche unpacks the prospects for employees when automation threatens jobs in a country with nearly 30% unemployment.

Script:


V/O: They call the epoch we live in the age of man, thanks (in no small part) to several industrial revolutions that have transformed society.

The first saw invention of the steam engine and the birth of mechanization

The second saw the harnessing of oil & electricity, the birth of industry and an age, factory assembly lines, cars & aeroplanes

The 3rd heralded a world of television, computers & the internet. The Digital Revolution

And now a 4th Industrial Revolution is once again transforming society. This is an age of AI & Machine Learning in which computers work & react like humans through complex algorithms to become truly intelligent machines.

V/O: Bronwyn Williams is a trend forecaster with a particular view of what this 4th industrial revolution will look like.

Bronwyn Williams: more from Bronwyn on 4IR

V/O: These are interesting times according to tech journalist Toby Shapshak

Toby Shapshak: on 4IR

MASA: Artificial intelligence has been a part of popular culture for decades thanks to the likes of Sci-Fi films Terminator and tv series like Westworld. They paint a picture of a future in which robots take over the world. Well the future is here but it’s not quite what you expected…

V/O: Dr Michael Grant is the chief technology officer at a Cape Town based company Data Prophet, which specialises in AI solutions for the manufacturing industry.

Dr Michael Grant: what does dataprophet do?

V/O: One of DataProphet’s biggest clients is Atlantis Foundries where it integrated deep-learning AI technology into production processes and managed to reduce manufacturing defects in engine blocks the Foundries produce for Daimler Mercedes.

V/O: CEO Mervyn Moodley explains why they needed an AI Solution.

Mervyn & Michael explain the case study, benefits, affect on jobs etc

V/O: But while 4IR has the potential to improve the quality of life for all, there has never been a time of greater promise or profound peril. The radical changes being wrought by technology are predicted to disrupt almost every industry in every country around the world.

Bronwyn on the potential for job losses

V/O: One sector already being affected is banking. Customer behaviour the world over is shifting towards accelerated adoption of digital services. As a result, the past 2 years has seen thousands of retrenchments as South African banks transition to a digital economy.

The digital disruption of banking led finance union SASBO to threaten industrial action for the first time since 1920. Joe Kokela is the Secretary General.

Joe Kokela: on why SASBO resorted to strike action and their approach to digitisation, on why they feel banks have not been fair to them, how they feel excluded from the conversation around digitisation & automation.

V/O: The strike was averted at the last minute when an urgent court interdict was granted to Business Unity South Africa, on the grounds that proper procedures weren’t followed. BUSA CEO Cas Coovadia explains that there have been consultations between the banks & SASBO.

Cas Coovadia on why they opposed the industrial action

V/O: While the strike was interdicted due to a technicality, the matter has not been resolved. The relationship between the union and the banks is still very acrimonious and the threat of strike action is still very much on the cards.
Joe Kokela on appealing the court interdict

V/O: So while the union may still get to take industrial action, it remains to be seen if it will have the desired effect.

Toby on the strike being self-defeating

V/O: So how will a solution be found?
Joe on what the union wants based on the research they did

Cas on the need for dialogue between banks, labour, government & education


V/O: The turmoil in the banking sector is just a taste of things to come. Jobs once considered safe may one day become redundant

Bronwyn on how AI will impact on Medicine, Law & Accounting

Brownyn, Toby & Michael on fit for future jobs
